ap_computer_science_a-f01.title: DigitTools: digit sums and the first Harshad number

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method digitSum, which returns the sum of the digits of the non-negative integer n. For example, digitSum(1305) returns 9 and digitSum(0) returns 0. Complete the method digitSum.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses a loop that continues while digits remain (n > 0) and ends for n = 0 without error; Isolates the last digit with n % 10 (not n / 10).
Removes the last digit from n with n / 10 after it has been used
common_errors: removes the digit before adding it

rubric_rows.criterion: Accumulates a running total that starts at 0 and is returned after the loop

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the method firstHarshad, which returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to start that is divisible by its own digit sum. You must use digitSum appropriately to receive full credit. For example, firstHarshad(11) returns 12, because 11 is not divisible by 2 and 12 is divisible by 1 + 2 = 3. Complete the method firstHarshad.

rubric_rows.criterion: Starts the search at start itself (so start can be the answer); Repeats until a qualifying value is found (loop with a stopping condition or an infinite loop with a return).
Calls digitSum with the candidate value as the argument
common_errors: recomputes the digit sum incorrectly instead of calling digitSum

rubric_rows.criterion: Tests divisibility of the candidate by its digit sum (k % digitSum(k) == 0, with the operands in this order)
common_errors: tests only whether k is even

rubric_rows.criterion: Returns the candidate number, not its digit sum

ap_computer_science_a-f02.title: Battery: a class that limits a charge level

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A Battery object keeps track of its charge level, a whole number from 0 through 100, and the number of times it has been recharged. The class has the following behavior: the constructor Battery(int startLevel) creates a battery with the given level and 0 recharges; use(int amount) lowers the level by amount but never below 0, and returns the amount that was actually used; recharge() sets the level to 100 and increases the number of recharges by 1; getLevel() and getCycles() return the current level and the number of recharges; isLow() returns true if the level is less than 20 and false otherwise. Assume that startLevel is between 0 and 100, inclusive, and that amount is not negative. Write the complete Battery class, including the instance variables, the constructor, and all methods.

rubric_rows.criterion: Declares the class header and private instance variables for the level and the recharge count; Constructor stores the starting level and starts with 0 recharges.
required_elements: private int level; private int cycles
common_errors: no variable for the recharge count

rubric_rows.criterion: use lowers the level by the amount when the level is large enough; use never lets the level fall below 0.
use returns the amount that was actually used (the limited amount, not the requested amount or the level)
recharge sets the level to 100
recharge increases the recharge count by 1
getLevel and getCycles return the current values with correct return types
isLow returns true exactly when the level is below 20 (a level of 20 is not low)

ap_computer_science_a-f03.title: NameList: keep only the first copy of each name

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method removeLaterDuplicates, which removes from the ArrayList names every String that is equal to an earlier String in names. Only the first occurrence of each String remains, and the order of the remaining Strings must not change. The method changes the list it is given rather than returning a new list. For example, if names is ["a", "b", "a", "c", "b"], then after the call names is ["a", "b", "c"]. Complete the method removeLaterDuplicates.

rubric_rows.criterion: Traverses the list positions with correct bounds based on names.size(), forward or backward, so that every position that could hold a later duplicate is examined; Reads an element with get(i).
required_elements: a loop over the valid indexes of names, in either direction

rubric_rows.criterion: Determines whether an equal String appears earlier (indexOf, a nested loop, or contains on a sublist); Compares Strings with equals (or indexOf), not ==.
required_elements: names.indexOf(s) < i or an inner loop with equals

rubric_rows.criterion: Removes the later duplicate (the element at index i or j), not the earlier occurrence; Handles the index shift after a removal (backward traversal or an index that does not advance after remove).
required_elements: backward loop or j not incremented after remove
common_errors: skips the element that moves into the removed position

rubric_rows.criterion: Keeps the first occurrence of every String (does not remove a String that appears only once); Keeps the remaining Strings in their original order.
Changes the original list instead of building and discarding a new list

ap_computer_science_a-f04.title: GridTools2: the smallest value in each column

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method columnMins, which returns a one-dimensional array whose element at index c is the smallest value in column c of grid. For example, if grid is { { 3, 8, 5 }, { 1, 9, 6 }, { 4, 7, 2 } } the method returns { 1, 7, 2 }. Complete the method columnMins.

rubric_rows.criterion: Creates a result array whose length equals the number of columns, grid[0].length; Iterates over every column with a loop bounded by the number of columns.

For each column, examines every row of that column (row index varies while the column index is fixed); Initializes the minimum from a value in the column (not 0 or a fixed constant that may be too small).
Replaces the current column minimum with a value only when that value is smaller (comparison direction is less-than); Includes every row, including the last row, in the comparison.
Stores each column's minimum at index c of the result array
Works for any rectangular size, including one row, one column, and negative values
required_elements: no assumption of square shape or positive values
common_errors: assumes the same number of rows and columns

rubric_rows.criterion: Returns the result array after the loops finish (return type int[])
